title: Changes in leaf mechanical properties under bending and tensile tests during dehydration in six plant species
text:
Follow the analysis
How do leaf mechanical properties change as leaves lose water? These notebooks follow three-point bending and tensile tests in six species, from instrument exports and sample measurements to the manuscript figures.
Figures 1–3 and the supplementary comparison use RWC of at least 60%. Models are generalized additive models (GAMs) fitted by restricted maximum likelihood (REML).

title: Changes in leaf mechanical properties under bending and tensile tests during dehydration in six plant species
text:
Integrate the measurements: combine the instrument exports with sample information and apply record exclusions.
Summarize the species: leaf thickness, leaf dry matter content (LDMC), and leaf mass per area (LMA).
Inspect bending properties, tensile properties, and their ratios as relative water content (RWC) decreases.
Compare stiffness changes between 100% and 80% RWC (manuscript Figure S2).

title: Changes in leaf mechanical properties under bending and tensile tests during dehydration in six plant species
text:
Reproduce the results
The data package contains 56 CP932 instrument CSV files and three metadata or exclusion CSV files. In the repository’s .Renviron, set PROJECT_DATA_DIR to the folder containing raw/ and manual/. Restart R, restore the packages with renv::restore(), and run quarto render from the repository root.
The first notebook generates the integrated tables; later notebooks read those tables and write their figures to outputs/figures/. Original inputs are not modified. See the repository README for environment setup and data requirements.

title: Changes in leaf mechanical properties under bending and tensile tests during dehydration in six plant species
text:
Scope
This site contains the main quantitative analyses and the stiffness comparison. Representative force–displacement examples (S1) are reproduced from the original selected IDs. Microscopy panels (S3) are not yet generated by the notebooks. Raw data and working manuscript files are not embedded in the site.

title: Data integration
text:
Analysis
Import the instrument exports, merge sample information, and apply the inherited record exclusions. Input files are read-only; the two integrated tables are written to outputs/tables/.
Code
source("R/setup.R")


Loading required package: nlme


This is mgcv 1.9-3. For overview type 'help("mgcv-package")'.


Code
filenames <- list.files(data_path("raw"), pattern = "\\.csv$", ignore.case = TRUE)
if (!length(filenames)) {
  stop("No raw CSV files found. Set PROJECT_DATA_DIR; see data/README.md.")
}
date <- sapply(filenames, function(x) strsplit(x, "_")[[1]][1])
type <- sapply(filenames, function(x) strsplit(x, "_")[[1]][2])
spp <- sapply(
  filenames,
  function(x) tools::file_path_sans_ext(strsplit(x, "_")[[1]][3])
)

# Data Integration ----
filepath <- file.path(data_path("raw"), filenames)
tensile_list <- list()
bending_list <- list()

for (i in seq_along(filepath)) {
  filename <- basename(tools::file_path_sans_ext(filepath[i])) # Get filename without extension
  cat(paste0(filename, "\n")) # Print filename to console
  d <- read.csv(filepath[i], fileEncoding = "cp932") # Read CSV file with Japanese encoding
  # Bending test
  if (d[1, 3] == "3点曲げ") {
    N <- which(d[, 1] == "名前")
    sample_info <- d[
      (N[1] + 2):(N[2] - ifelse(d[N[2] - 1, 1] == "", 2, 1)),
      1:4
    ]
    result <- d[
      (N[2] + 3):(N[2] + (diff(N) - ifelse(d[N[2] - 1, 1] == "", 1, 0))),
      1:4
    ]
    res <- cbind(sample_info, result)
    names(res) <- c(
      "ID1",
      "thick",
      "width",
      "span",
      "ID2",
      "Fmax",
      "DISmax",
      "E"
    )
    res$filename <- filename
    res$date <- strsplit(filename, "_")[[1]][1]
    res$spp <- strsplit(filename, "_")[[1]][3]
    res$spp <- spp[i]
    bending_list[[filename]] <- res
  }

  # Tensile test
  if (d[1, 3] == "引張") {
    N <- which(d[, 1] == "名前")
    sample_info <- d[
      (N[1] + 2):(N[2] - ifelse(d[N[2] - 1, 1] == "", 2, 1)),
      1:4
    ]
    result <- d[
      (N[2] + 3):(N[2] + (diff(N)) - ifelse(d[N[2] - 1, 1] == "", 1, 0)),
      1:4
    ]
    res <- cbind(sample_info, result)
    names(res) <- c(
      "ID1",
      "thick",
      "width",
      "span",
      "ID2",
      "E",
      "strength",
      "strain"
    )
    res$filename <- filename
    res$date <- strsplit(filename, "_")[[1]][1]
    res$spp <- strsplit(filename, "_")[[1]][3]
    res$spp <- spp[i]
    tensile_list[[filename]] <- res
  }
}
d_bending <- do.call(rbind, bending_list) # Combine all bending test data into a single data frame
d_tensile <- do.call(rbind, tensile_list) # Combine all tensile test data into a single data frame


# Data cleaning ----
d_bending$ID <- sub("_", "", d_bending$ID1) # Remove underscore from ID
d_bending$ID <- sub("f|b", "", d_bending$ID) # Remove leaf side indicator from ID
d_bending$leaf_side <- ifelse(grepl("f", d_bending$ID1), "f", "b") # adaxial or abaxial
d_bending$leaf_side <- ifelse(d_bending$leaf_side == "f", "adaxial", "abaxial")
d_tensile <- d_tensile[-which(d_tensile$ID1 == "failed"), ] # Remove rows where tensile test failed
# Remove rows where tensile test failed
d_tensile <- d_tensile[
  -which(d_tensile$ID1 == 31 & d_tensile$spp == "youshuyamagobou"),
]
d_tensile <- d_tensile[
  -which(d_tensile$ID1 == 39 & d_tensile$spp == "youshuyamagobou"),
]
# Remove rows with empty E values
d_bending <- d_bending[-which(d_bending$E == "-.-"), ]

# Merging data with sample information ----
d_info_bending <- read.csv(data_path("manual", "bending_sample_information.csv"))
d_info_tensile <- read.csv(data_path("manual", "tensile_sample_information.csv"))
# rename column names
names(d_info_bending) <- c(
  "ID",
  "leaf_side",
  "dry_time",
  "turgid_weight",
  "fresh_weight",
  "thickness",
  "width",
  "length",
  "F_max",
  "DIS_max",
  "E",
  "dry_weight",
  "water_content",
  "I",
  "EI",
  "area",
  "water_weight",
  "liquid",
  "solid",
  "air",
  "air_fraction",
  "date",
  "thickness_TW", # leaf thickness at turgid weight
  "spp"
)
names(d_info_tensile) <- c(
  "ID",
  "dry_time",
  "turgid_weight",
  "fresh_weight",
  "thickness",
  "width",
  "length",
  "E",
  "F_max",
  "DIS_max",
  "dry_weight",
  "water_content",
  "I",
  "EI",
  "area",
  "water_weight",
  "liquid",
  "solid",
  "air",
  "air_fraction",
  "date",
  "thickness_TW", # leaf thickness at turgid weight
  "spp"
)
d_info_bending$leaf_side <- ifelse(
  d_info_bending$leaf_side == "front",
  "adaxial",
  "abaxial"
)

# Merge
data_list <- list()
data_list[["bending"]] <- merge(
  d_bending,
  d_info_bending,
  by = c("spp", "leaf_side", "ID"),
  all = TRUE
)
data_list[["tensile"]] <- merge(
  d_tensile,
  d_info_tensile,
  by.x = c("spp", "ID1"),
  by.y = c("spp", "ID")
)

# Data cleaning ----
df_excluded <- read.csv(data_path("manual", "exclude_records_bending.csv"))
# 除外キー（species, id）の組を作って %in% で除く
keep_bending <- !do.call(paste, data_list[["bending"]][c("spp", "ID")]) %in%
  do.call(paste, df_excluded[c("species", "id")])
df_bending_filtered <- data_list[["bending"]][keep_bending, ]
keep_tensile <- !do.call(paste, data_list[["tensile"]][c("spp", "ID1")]) %in%
  do.call(paste, df_excluded[c("species", "id")])
df_tensile_filtered <- data_list[["tensile"]][keep_tensile, ]

# Save data ----
write.csv(
  df_bending_filtered,
  "outputs/tables/bending.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
write.csv(
  df_tensile_filtered,
  "outputs/tables/tensile.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

Analysis

data_list <- list()
data_list[["bending"]] <- read.csv("outputs/tables/bending.csv")
data_list[["tensile"]] <- read.csv("outputs/tables/tensile.csv")


# Leaf thickness ----
# Extract data at 100% RWC
# Remove rows where dry_time is NA​

  !is.na(data_list[["bending"]]$dry_time),
]
# Extract rows where dry_time = 0

]
data_list[["tensile_turgid"]] <- data_list[["tensile"]][

title: Figure 1: Bending properties
text:
Analysis
Fit generalized additive models (GAMs) to bending stiffness, Young’s modulus, and the second moment of area. The analysis uses relative water content (RWC) of at least 60%, matching the main manuscript figures.
Code
source("R/setup.R")


Loading required package: nlme


This is mgcv 1.9-3. For overview type 'help("mgcv-package")'.


Code
# Load data
df_list <- list()
df_list[["bending"]] <- read.csv("outputs/tables/bending.csv")
df_list[["tensile"]] <- read.csv("outputs/tables/tensile.csv")

categories <- c("bending", "tensile")
df <- df_list[[categories[1]]]
df <- df[df$water_content >= 60, ] # filter data for water content >= 60%
df$EI <- df$EI * 1000 # convert unit of EI
df$I <- df$I * 1000 # convert unit of I
spp <- c(
  "ubayuri",
  "youshuyamagobou",
  "yurinoki",
  "niseakashia",
  "aoki",
  "nezumimochi"
) # species names
names(spp) <- c(
  "Cardiocrinum_cordatum",
  "Phytolacca_americana",
  "Liriodendron_tulipifera",
  "Robinia_pseudoacacia",
  "Aucuba_japonica",
  "Ligustrum lucidum"
)
pred_range <- c(60, 100) # Prediction range
xlim <- c(100, 60) # Reverse x-axis
mar <- c(5, 5, 0.5, 0.5) # Margins


# Plot GAM with confidence intervals ----
output_dir <- "outputs/figures/figure_01"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
  dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

# (A) - (F) RWC vs EI
lapply(seq_along(spp), function(i) {
  sp <- spp[i]
  df_sp <- df[df$spp == sp, ]
  df_adaxial <- droplevels(subset(df_sp, leaf_side == "adaxial"))
  df_abaxial <- droplevels(subset(df_sp, leaf_side == "abaxial"))
  output_path <- file.path(
    output_dir,
    paste0(LETTERS[i], "_RWC_vs_EI_", names(spp)[i], ".svg")
  )
  svg(output_path, bg = "transparent")
  # Plot adaxial side
  plot_gam_ci(
    data = df_adaxial,
    x = "water_content",
    y = "EI",
    ylim = gam_ci_ylim(df_sp, "water_content", "EI", pred_range),
    side = "adaxial",
    pred_range = pred_range,
    xlim = xlim,
    mar = mar
  )
  # Add abaxial side to the same plot
  plot_gam_ci(
    data = df_abaxial,
    x = "water_content",
    y = "EI",
    side = "abaxial",
    pred_range = pred_range,
    xlim = xlim,
    mar = mar,
    add = TRUE, # add to existing plot
    pch = 22 # Use different point shape for abaxial
  )
  dev.off()
})

# (G) - (L) RWC vs E
lapply(seq_along(spp), function(i) {
  sp <- spp[i]
  df_sp <- df[df$spp == sp, ]
  df_adaxial <- droplevels(subset(df_sp, leaf_side == "adaxial"))
  df_abaxial <- droplevels(subset(df_sp, leaf_side == "abaxial"))
  output_path <- file.path(
    output_dir,
    paste0(LETTERS[6 + i], "_RWC_vs_E_", names(spp)[i], ".svg")
  )
  svg(output_path, bg = "transparent")
  # Plot adaxial side
  plot_gam_ci(
    data = df_adaxial,
    x = "water_content",
    y = "E.x",
    ylim = gam_ci_ylim(df_sp, "water_content", "E.x", pred_range),
    side = "adaxial",
    pred_range = pred_range,
    xlim = xlim,
    mar = mar
  )
  # Add abaxial side to the same plot
  plot_gam_ci(
    data = df_abaxial,
    x = "water_content",
    y = "E.x",
    side = "abaxial",
    pred_range = pred_range,
    xlim = xlim,
    mar = mar,
    add = TRUE, # add to existing plot
    pch = 22
  )
  dev.off()
})

# (M) - (R) RWC vs I
lapply(seq_along(spp), function(i) {
  sp <- spp[i]
  df_sp <- df[df$spp == sp, ]
  df_adaxial <- droplevels(subset(df_sp, leaf_side == "adaxial"))
  df_abaxial <- droplevels(subset(df_sp, leaf_side == "abaxial"))
  output_path <- file.path(
    output_dir,
    paste0(LETTERS[6 * 2 + i], "_RWC_vs_I_", names(spp)[i], ".svg")
  )
  svg(output_path, bg = "transparent")
  # Plot adaxial side
  plot_gam_ci(
    data = df_adaxial,

Reading the results
日本語はこちら（JP）
All 102 GAMs underlying Figures 1–3 and S2 are refitted using the figure inputs, units, exclusions, and settings. Inputs are outputs/tables/bending.csv and tensile.csv; outputs are the CSV and RDS below. After data integration, run quarto render notebook/10-gam-results.qmd from the project root. No cache is used.
Each model fits a response as an intercept plus a smooth function of RWC and error, separately by species, trait, and bending direction. Models use the Gaussian family, identity link, the existing default s(RWC) specification, and REML smoothing selection. Figure 3 uses mean bending and tensile RWC.
The approximate p-value tests the null hypothesis that the RWC smooth is zero throughout. It does not test monotonic increase or decrease, nonlinearity alone, species or direction differences, or whether a ratio differs from 1 or 3. A nonsignificant result does not establish absence of change.
All p-values are unadjusted. Test families and multiplicity handling for the manuscript remain undecided. Interpret curves, effect sizes, and uncertainty together rather than counting significant results. This summary does not establish that residual assumptions or basis dimensions are adequate.
Main figures and S2 use RWC ≥60%. Figure 3 requires both measurements to meet the cutoff. The S2 abaxial GAM for Ligustrum lucidum is included, although its subsequent stiffness decrease and contribution to the species-level regression are excluded in the existing analysis. S2’s two species-level regressions are not GAMs and are not included here.

title: Appendix C — Shared functions
text:
plot_gam_ci <- function(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  side = c("adaxial", "abaxial", "tensile"),
  pred_range = NULL, # Prediction range; if NULL, use data range
  n_pred = 200, # Number of prediction points
  xlim = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  pch = 21,
  cex_pt = 1.8,
  draw_points = TRUE,
  ci_alpha = 0.12, # Transparency of CI band
  pt_fill_alpha = 0.5, # Transparency of points
  pt_border_alpha = 0.9, # Transparency of point borders
  line_alpha = 0.9, # Transparency of regression line
  line_lwd = 4,
  ci_lty = 2, # Line type for CI boundaries
  mar = c(3, 3, 0, 0), # Margins
  xaxt = "s",
  yaxt = "s",
  xlab = "",
  ylab = "",
  cex.axis = 2.5, # Axis label size
  cex.lab = 2.5, # Axis label size
  axis_lwd = 1, # Axis and tick line width
  mgp_x = c(3, 1.5, 0),
  mgp_y = c(3, 0.5, 0), # Margins for axis labels
  add = FALSE, # Add to an existing plot
  ...
) {
  # Check arguments
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(data), is.character(x), is.character(y))
  side <- match.arg(side)

  # --- inherit axes when add=TRUE ---
  if (isTRUE(add)) {
    usr <- par("usr") # c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
    if (is.null(xlim)) {
      xlim <- usr[1:2]
    }
    if (is.null(ylim)) ylim <- usr[3:4]
  }

  # ---- Color settings (according to user's preference) ----
  if (side == "adaxial") {
    base_col <- 7 # In the user's environment, red
  } else if (side == "abaxial") {
    base_col <- 6 # In the user's environment, blue
  } else {
    base_col <- 1 # For tensile, gray
  }
  # Semi-transparent color for filling (CI band & point fill)
  fill_col <- adjustcolor(base_col, alpha.f = ci_alpha) # CI band fill color
  pt_fill <- adjustcolor(base_col, alpha.f = pt_fill_alpha) # Point fill color
  pt_border <- adjustcolor(base_col, alpha.f = pt_border_alpha) # Point border color
  line_col <- adjustcolor(base_col, alpha.f = line_alpha) # Line color
  ci_col <- fill_col # CI band color

  # ---- Prepare data ----
  df_gam <- data[, c(x, y)]
  # Model
  fml <- as.formula(paste(y, "~ s(", x, ")"))
  model_gam <- mgcv::gam(
    formula = fml,
    data = df_gam,
    method = "REML",
    na.action = na.exclude
  )

  # Prediction range
  if (is.null(pred_range)) {
    xr <- range(df_gam[[x]], na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    xr <- pred_range
  }
  new_x <- setNames(
    data.frame(seq(from = xr[1], to = xr[2], length.out = n_pred)),
    x
  )

  # Prediction
  pred <- predict(model_gam, newdata = new_x, se.fit = TRUE)
  ci_lo <- pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit
  ci_hi <- pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit

  # Order for plotting
  ord <- order(new_x[[x]])

  # ---- Axis ranges ----
  if (is.null(ylim)) {
    # Range including observations and CI
    yr <- c(0, max(c(df_gam[[y]], ci_lo, ci_hi), na.rm = TRUE))
    #pad <- diff(yr) * 0.05 # Padding for upper limit
    #ylim <- c(yr[1], yr[2] + pad) # Add padding to the upper limit
    ylim <- yr
  }
  if (is.null(xlim)) {
    xlim <- range(new_x[[x]], na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  # --- clip prediction to visible x-range ---
  xmin <- min(xlim)
  xmax <- max(xlim)
  keep <- which(new_x[[x]] >= xmin & new_x[[x]] <= xmax)
  # 予測点が全て範囲外なら何もしないで返す
  if (length(keep) < 2) {
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  xk <- new_x[[x]][keep] # x values to keep
  fik <- pred$fit[keep] # Predicted values
  lok <- ci_lo[keep] # CI lower bounds
  hik <- ci_hi[keep] # CI lower and upper bounds
  ordk <- order(xk) # Order for plotting

  # ---- Set up plot background ----
  if (!add) {
    op <- par(mar = mar, xpd = FALSE) # Set margins and allow clipping
    on.exit(par(op), add = TRUE) # Restore original parameters
    plot(
      NA,
      NA,
      xlim = xlim,
      ylim = ylim,
      xlab = xlab,
      ylab = ylab,
      xaxt = "n",
      yaxt = "n",
      ...
    )
    # Axes (customize if needed)
    if (xaxt != "n") {
      axis(
        1,
        at = pretty(new_x[[x]]),
        labels = pretty(new_x[[x]]),
        cex.axis = cex.axis,
        mgp = mgp_x, lwd = axis_lwd, lwd.ticks = axis_lwd
      )
    }
    if (yaxt != "n") {
      axis(2, at = pretty(ylim), las = 2, cex.axis = cex.axis, mgp = mgp_y,
           lwd = axis_lwd, lwd.ticks = axis_lwd)
    }
    if (xlab != "") {
      mtext(xlab, side = 1, line = mgp_x[1], cex = cex.lab)
    }
    if (ylab != "") mtext(ylab, side = 2, line = mgp_y[1], cex = cex.lab)
  }

  # ---- Draw in order: CI band → CI boundary lines → regression line → points ----
  polygon(
    c(xk[ordk], rev(xk[ordk])),
    c(lok[ordk], rev(hik[ordk])),
    col = ci_col,
    border = NA
  )
  lines(xk[ordk], lok[ordk], lty = ci_lty, col = line_col)
  lines(xk[ordk], hik[ordk], lty = ci_lty, col = line_col)
  lines(xk[ordk], fik[ordk], col = line_col, lwd = line_lwd)

  if (draw_points) {
    points(
      df_gam[[x]],
      df_gam[[y]],
      pch = pch,
      cex = cex_pt,
      col = pt_border,
      bg = pt_fill
    )
  }

  invisible(list(
    model = model_gam,
    newdata = new_x,
    fit = pred$fit,
    se = pred$se.fit,
    ci_lo = ci_lo,
    ci_hi = ci_hi,
    side = side,
    colors = list(base = base_col, line = line_col, fill = fill_col)
  ))
}

# Shared limits for separately fitted adaxial and abaxial curves.
gam_ci_ylim <- function(data, x, y, pred_range, n_pred = 200) {
  new_x <- setNames(data.frame(seq(pred_range[1], pred_range[2],
                                   length.out = n_pred)), x)
  values <- c(0, data[[y]])
  for (side_data in split(data, data$leaf_side, drop = TRUE)) {
    model <- mgcv::gam(as.formula(paste(y, "~ s(", x, ")")),
                       data = side_data[, c(x, y)], method = "REML",
                       na.action = na.exclude)
    prediction <- predict(model, newdata = new_x, se.fit = TRUE)
    values <- c(values, prediction$fit - 1.96 * prediction$se.fit,
                prediction$fit + 1.96 * prediction$se.fit)
  }
  range(values, finite = TRUE)
}

text:
Tensile stiffness
add_tensile_stiffness() calculates the cross-sectional area from the instrument dimensions and multiplies it by the instrument Young’s modulus. This keeps Figures 2, 3, S2, and the submission PDFs on the same definition of \(E_t A\).
Download add_tensile_stiffness.R
# Use the instrument dimensions associated with the instrument Young's modulus.
# E.x is in MPa = N/mm^2; thick and width.x are in mm; EA is in N.
add_tensile_stiffness <- function(data) {
  stopifnot(all(c("E.x", "thick", "width.x") %in% names(data)))
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(data$E.x)), all(is.finite(data$thick)),
            all(is.finite(data$width.x)), all(data$thick > 0),
            all(data$width.x > 0))
  data$cross_section_area <- data$thick * data$width.x
  data$EA <- data$E.x * data$cross_section_area
  data
}

title: Appendix D — Figures for journal submission
text:
Preparation
The code below generates a vector PDF for journal submission and a 600 dpi PNG for preview or preprint preparation, for each manuscript figure. Expand Show generation code to inspect each step. The PDFs use the same inputs, exclusions, GAMs, and prediction grids as the analysis chapters; only the panel layout and typography change. Figure S1 uses the fixed examples and baseline correction from its reproduction chapter. Both formats are downloadable rather than embedded on this page.
Download the generation notebook (QMD)
The original layout is retained: six species rows, traits in columns, and square plotting regions. Figures 1, 2, and 3 are 120, 155, and 85.5 mm wide, respectively. Their heights are calculated from the panel widths and margins (approximately 235, 228, and 231 mm). Using a figure-specific width within the journal’s 178 mm limit avoids excessively tall figures without rearranging panels. Panel letters and the association between species, traits, and fitted curves are unchanged. Species names are italic, and y labels are shared within each trait column. Figure S2 retains its 120 × 120 mm plot with regression annotations inside it. All figures use Arial at a 9 pt base size, 8.55 pt tick labels/legends, and 8.1 pt species names and compact regression annotations. The PDFs retain vector lines and text. Corrected \(E_t A\) values and units are retained.
For journal submission, keep the main text in a DOCX/ODT file without the figure images, retain the figure legends at the end of that file, and submit each main figure as an individual PDF. Separate files are also allowed at initial submission. Supporting information follows its own instructions; the journal recommends a combined PDF with its figures, legends, tables, title, and authors where possible.
For a preview or preprint version, insert the PNGs using Insert → Pictures, keep the aspect ratio, and disable Word image compression. The PNGs contain 600 pixels per inch at the intended dimensions. Reduce them if necessary to leave room for captions; enlarging them lowers the effective resolution. Export the figure-containing document to PDF as needed for the selected preprint service.
PDF lines and text remain vector objects, so increasing the page size does not add detail. We use the intended manuscript dimensions for both output formats, without a PDF enlargement step or additional output dependencies. Final printed width and lettering still matter: the journal specifies widths up to 178 mm and lettering of 8–12 pt. Check the figures at their intended printed dimensions before submission. See the journal guidelines.
Tensile stiffness is calculated as E_t * A, with A = thick * width.x from the instrument dimensions (mm) associated with E.x (MPa). The resulting EA is in N; bending-to-tensile stiffness ratios are in mm².
Run data integration first. Figure S2 also requires the stiffness comparison chapter, which saves its data and fitted regressions without refitting here. Figure S1 requires 11-force-displacement.qmd, which saves its original examples.

# Draw manuscript panels using the same GAM function as the analysis chapters.
plot_submission_panels <- function(data, species, metrics, labels, file,
                                   x = "water_content", tensile = FALSE,
                                   reference_lines = NULL, label_offsets = NULL) {
  width_mm <- switch(as.character(length(metrics)), "2" = 85.5, "3" = 120, "4" = 155)
  stopifnot(!is.null(width_mm))
  # Horizontal offsets from each column's left edge, as fractions of page width.
  if (is.null(label_offsets)) {
    label_offsets <- rep(if (length(metrics) == 2L) 4 / width_mm else 2.5 / width_mm,
                         length(metrics))
  }
  stopifnot(length(label_offsets) == length(metrics), all(is.finite(label_offsets)))
  # Keep the original species rows, trait columns, and square plotting regions.
  margins <- c(1.3, 3.1, 1.6, 0.3)
  if (length(metrics) == 2L) margins[2] <- 4
  line_mm <- 9 / 72 * 25.4 * 1.2
  panel_mm <- width_mm / length(metrics) - sum(margins[c(2, 4)]) * line_mm
  height_mm <- length(species) * (panel_mm + sum(margins[c(1, 3)]) * line_mm) +
    1.8 * line_mm
  panels <- matrix(seq_len(length(species) * length(metrics)), nrow = length(species))
  # Match the orange/blue appearance of the embedded manuscript figures.

  manuscript_palette[c(6, 7)] <- c("#2977B5", "#D7673B")
  palette(manuscript_palette)
  on.exit(palette(original_palette), add = TRUE)
  cairo_pdf(file, width = width_mm / 25.4, height = height_mm / 25.4,
            family = "Arial", pointsize = 9, bg = "white")
  on.exit(dev.off(), add = TRUE)
  draw <- function() {
    layout(panels)
    par(mar = margins, oma = c(1.8, 0, 0, 0), tcl = -0.2,
        pty = "s", cex = 1, lwd = 0.5, fg = "black", col.axis = "black")
    results <- list()
    plot_regions <- list()
    for (j in seq_along(metrics)) {
      for (i in seq_along(species)) {
        subset_data <- data[data$spp == species[i], ]
        sides <- if (tensile) "tensile" else c("adaxial", "abaxial")
        ylim <- if (tensile) NULL else
          gam_ci_ylim(subset_data, x, metrics[j], c(60, 100))
        for (side in sides) {
          side_data <- if (tensile) subset_data else
            droplevels(subset(subset_data, leaf_side == side))
          results[[length(results) + 1L]] <- plot_gam_ci(
            data = side_data, x = x, y = metrics[j], side = side,
            pred_range = c(60, 100), xlim = c(100, 60), ylim = ylim, mar = margins,
            add = side == "abaxial", pch = if (side == "abaxial") 22 else 21,
            cex_pt = 0.75, pt_border_alpha = 0.5, line_lwd = 1.2,
            cex.axis = 0.95, cex.lab = 1, axis_lwd = 0.5, xaxt = "n",
            ci_lty = 3, mgp_x = c(1.7, 0.4, 0), mgp_y = c(2.5, 0.3, 0))
          if (!is.null(reference_lines) && metrics[j] == "E_ratio") {
            abline(h = reference_lines, lty = 2, lwd = 0.7)
          }
        }
        axis(1, at = seq(100, 60, -10), cex.axis = 0.95, gap.axis = 0.5,
             mgp = c(1.7, 0.4, 0), lwd = 0.5, lwd.ticks = 0.5)
        panel <- LETTERS[(j - 1L) * length(species) + i]
        usr <- par("usr")
        text(usr[1] + 0.025 * diff(usr[1:2]),
             usr[4] - 0.025 * diff(usr[3:4]), paste0("(", panel, ")"),
             adj = c(0, 1), cex = 1, col = "black")
        if (i == 1L && j == 1L && !tensile) {
          legend("topright", c("Adaxial", "Abaxial"), pch = c(21, 22),
                 pt.bg = adjustcolor(c(7, 6), alpha.f = 0.5), col = c(7, 6),
                 pt.cex = 0.9, cex = 0.95, bg = "white", box.col = "black",
                 text.col = "black")
        }
        # Store physical plot rectangles for layout checks.
        plot_regions[[length(plot_regions) + 1L]] <- c(
          row = i, column = j,
          width = par("pin")[1], height = par("pin")[2],
          left = grconvertX(usr[1], "user", "ndc"),
          top = grconvertY(usr[4], "user", "ndc"))
      }
    }
    # One shared y label per column, and species names above the first column.
    layout(1)
    par(fig = c(0, 1, 0, 1), mar = rep(0, 4), oma = rep(0, 4),
        pty = "m", plt = c(0, 1, 0, 1), new = TRUE)
    plot.new()
    plot.window(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
    for (j in seq_along(metrics)) {
      text((j - 1L) / length(metrics) + label_offsets[j], 0.5,
           labels[[j]], srt = 90, cex = 1, col = "black")
    }
    for (i in seq_along(species)) {
      region <- plot_regions[[i]]
      text(region["left"], region["top"] + 0.008,
           names(species)[i], adj = c(0, 0), font = 3, cex = 0.9,
           col = "black", xpd = NA)
    }
    text(0.5, 0.006, "Relative water content (%)", adj = c(0.5, 0), col = "black")
    attr(results, "plot_regions") <- do.call(rbind, plot_regions)
    invisible(results)
  }
  results <- draw()
  png_results <- save_submission_png(file, width_mm / 25.4, height_mm / 25.4, 9, draw)
  attr(results, "png_plot_regions") <- attr(png_results, "plot_regions")
  invisible(results)
}

plot_submission_comparison <- function(comparison, file) {
  data <- comparison$data
  cairo_pdf(file, width = 120 / 25.4, height = 120 / 25.4,
            family = "Arial", pointsize = 9, bg = "white")
  on.exit(dev.off(), add = TRUE)
  draw <- function() {
    par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1), mgp = c(2.5, 0.6, 0), cex = 1)
    # Include negative decreases (predicted stiffness increases) in the plot.
    plot_limits <- range(c(0, 100, unlist(data[, c(
      "drop_tensile", "drop_adaxial", "drop_abaxial")])), na.rm = TRUE)
    plot(data$drop_tensile, data$drop_adaxial, type = "n", asp = 1,
         xlim = plot_limits, ylim = plot_limits,
         xlab = "Tensile stiffness decrease (%)",
         ylab = "Bending stiffness decrease (%)")
    abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
    for (side in c("adaxial", "abaxial")) {
      colour <- if (side == "adaxial") 7 else 6
      points(data$drop_tensile, data[[paste0("drop_", side)]],
             pch = if (side == "adaxial") 21 else 22, cex = 1.2,
             bg = adjustcolor(colour, alpha.f = 0.5),
             col = adjustcolor(colour, alpha.f = 0.9))
      abline(comparison[[side]], col = adjustcolor(colour, alpha.f = 0.9), lwd = 1.5)
    }
    legend("topleft", c("Adaxial", "Abaxial"), pch = c(21, 22),
           pt.bg = adjustcolor(c(7, 6), alpha.f = 0.5), col = c(7, 6),
           cex = 0.95, bty = "n")
    annotation <- vapply(c("adaxial", "abaxial"), function(side) {
      model <- comparison[[side]]
      statistics <- summary(model)
      sprintf("%s: y = %.3fx %+.3f; R\u00b2 = %.3f; p = %.4f",
              side, coef(model)[2], coef(model)[1], statistics$r.squared,
              coef(statistics)[2, 4])
    }, character(1))
    legend("bottomright", annotation, text.col = c(7, 6), cex = 0.9, bty = "n")
  }
  draw()
  save_submission_png(file, 120 / 25.4, 120 / 25.4, 9, draw)
}
